docs.text: ATSAnomaly anomaly detection ¶ Suitable for building a memory bank from normal OK images only, then identifying new images that deviate from the normal distribution. The current implementation uses the PatchCore method, without multi-epoch gradient training as in ordinary classification. Training and calibration data ¶ Training and independent calibration directories must contain only OK images. If calibration is blank, images are deduplicated by content and approximately 20% is held out using fixed random seed 42; at least 3 distinct images are required. Calibration images do not enter the memory bank; content duplicates between training and independent calibration cause an error. Thresholds estimated only from OK images cannot establish defect recall, false-positive rate or production accuracy. Validate business performance using independent OK/NG samples. Construction parameters ¶ Parameter Effect Backbone ResNet18 (faster) or Wide ResNet50-2 (higher capacity), using bundled pretrained weights with frozen parameters. Image size Default 256; resizes the whole image to a square without center-cropping edges, potentially changing aspect ratio; 64–1024 and a multiple of 32 Extraction batch size Default 2, range 1–16; controls feature extraction batch size; reduce if GPU memory is insufficient Coreset retention fraction Default 0.01; fraction of candidate features retained, not the fraction of training images retained Candidate feature limit Default 50000; bounded sampling above this limit caps candidates entering coreset selection Coreset feature limit Default 5000; caps the final memory bank feature count The final coreset size is min(coreset feature limit, max(1, int(candidate feature count × retention fraction))) . Larger memory banks and image sizes generally increase RAM, GPU memory and inference computation requirements. This page has no learning rate, optimizer, epochs or early stopping settings. Progress consists of normal feature extraction, coreset sampling and OK threshold calibration. Thresholds and inference ¶ The model is saved as model.patchcore.pt . Use Anomaly inference validation on this page for inference, with a single image or image folder. Anomaly scores are feature distances, not probabilities, and need not be within 0–1. During construction, OK calibration scores estimate image-level and pixel-level thresholds. The inference threshold multiplier defaults to 1: below 1 is more sensitive; above 1 is more permissive. An image score reaching the image threshold is classified as NG; the pixel threshold determines the pixel mask. These are different statistics. Results include OK/NG, anomaly scores, heatmaps, overlays, masks, raw score maps and JSON/CSV. The output directory must not be inside the input image directory, preventing generated results from becoming inputs again. This model format is not a generic ONNX, ordinary classification PT or classic inference model; do not select it on the main Model inference validation page. CPU and single NVIDIA GPU execution both use the independent anomaly detection environment. See the anomaly parameter table for complete ranges.

docs.text: Dataset preparation ¶ Modern object detection, instance segmentation and oriented object detection ¶ Select the dataset root containing data.yaml ; the oriented detection page also accepts a YAML path. YAML specifies training, validation and class mapping. Images and labels must correspond; class IDs start at 0 and match the class list. dataset/ data.yaml images/train/ images/val/ labels/train/ labels/val/ Task Label contents: one object per line Standard detection class_id center_x center_y width height Instance segmentation class_id x1 y1 x2 y2 … , an object's contour polygon Oriented object detection class_id x1 y1 x2 y2 x3 y3 x4 y4 , four corners Normalize coordinates to 0–1. OBB corners must run clockwise or counterclockwise. Ordinary five-column boxes, raw DOTA labels and self-intersecting quadrilaterals are not valid OBB input. The software checks labels and reports file and line numbers. Modern classification ¶ Organize training/validation images by class, using the corresponding subfolder names as class names. Explicit train/class_name and val/class_name folders are recommended; the classification engine reads them according to its dataset rules. This page does not import classic classification TXT lists. classification/ train/OK/... train/NG/... val/OK/... val/NG/... Classification results are written beside the dataset in dataset-name_runs, preventing results from being treated as a class. Keep old result folders out of class directories. Classic object detection: one COCO folder ¶ COCO mode is selected by default. Select the dataset root and click Check dataset. The software recognizes training images, COCO JSON, classes and an optional independent validation set. A typical layout is: coco/ images/train/... images/val/... # optional annotations/train.json annotations/val.json # optional Without an independent validation set, all training images are used for training, with no automatic split or mAP calculation. OK background images may have no boxes: keep their image records without fabricating entries in annotations or creating an OK object class. The software retains these negative samples. Class mapping is based on the training annotations; training and validation class names must match. The software creates annotation copies and a class list inside the experiment without changing the original COCO files. Classic classification: one dataset folder ¶ Read train_list.txt , val_list.txt and Label.txt first; without lists, detect train/class_name and val/class_name . Preserve the existing split without automatic resplitting. Class IDs must be contiguous, and validation classes must belong to the training classes. For other folder naming conventions, first run Check dataset and inspect recognized counts and classes. Do not invent class IDs to bypass validation. Anomaly detection: OK images and independent calibration ¶ Include only OK images in the training directory. An independent OK calibration directory is optional; if blank, approximately 20% is held out after content-based deduplication, requiring at least 3 distinct OK images. Calibration images are excluded from the memory bank; content duplicates between training and calibration are rejected. This automatic holdout rule applies only to anomaly detection, not classic COCO detection.

docs.text: Feedback and progress tracking ¶ Feedback at the bottom of the sidebar submits problems to technical support. Submission, attachment uploads and progress queries require Internet access. Draft editing, local history and screenshot previews work offline. Description and attachments ¶ Choose a feedback type and describe the problem, reproduction steps and expected result. The description accepts up to 30000 characters; contact information is optional and limited to 500 characters. Include system information is enabled by default. It collects the application version, operating system, CPU, RAM, GPU model and memory, graphics driver and main application dependency versions without starting training engines. It does not actively collect machine codes, license keys, usernames or datasets. Include training logs is enabled by default. It includes the current console and existing engine.log , results.csv and training_metrics.jsonl from the selected experiment. The most recently registered experiment is selected by default; Current console log only can also be selected. Only the latest approximately 256 KB of each file is captured. Original files remain unchanged; models and training images are not uploaded. Common local paths and credentials are automatically hidden in logs, but not every sensitive value can be recognized. Inspect the preview before submitting, and uncheck logs or system information if unnecessary. Select local images or paste screenshots from the clipboard. Double-click the attachment list to preview, or remove an attachment. Up to 4 images are converted to PNG; images with a long edge above 4096 pixels are reduced, and each processed image is limited to 4 MB. Preview and submission ¶ Click Preview and submit feedback, inspect contact details, system information, log contents and the screenshot list, then click Confirm submission. Cancelling the preview uploads nothing to the feedback platform; the draft and preview record remain local. Attachments upload before feedback is created. Visibility of the description and attachments depends on the feedback platform's permissions; this is not a private chat. The form is locked during submission to prevent changes. Cancellation can be requested, but the current network request must finish first. History and progress ¶ History contains only this computer's records: feedback number, submission status, last sync time, description and synchronized replies. Drafts and records are stored in the current user's local application data directory and persist after closing the software. After successful submission, Check progress retrieves the corresponding feedback's status and replies. States include Received, In progress, Closed and Rejected. Closed does not mean the software verified that the problem was solved. Technical support handles feedback and replies; the client does not generate handling conclusions automatically. At most the first 100 replies are retrieved. Contact technical support for the complete record. Records with failed uploads or definite submission failures can be reviewed and retried. Successfully uploaded attachments are reused rather than uploaded again. If creating feedback times out, loses its connection or returns an ambiguous response, the record shows Needs verification and cannot be blindly resubmitted. Contact technical support to confirm the outcome. If it was created, use Link feedback number to enter the number provided by support; the software verifies that it belongs to this local feedback before linking it and querying progress. Exit is blocked while a feedback operation is running. Cancel or wait for completion before closing. A normal exit saves the current draft.

docs.text: Quick start ¶ Choose modern architectures, classic architectures or anomaly detection for the task. Use classification to identify classes, detection for ordinary boxes, instance segmentation for masks, and oriented detection for boxes with orientation. Prepare the appropriate dataset format. Classic detection and classification need one dataset folder; modern tasks each require their own label format. Select model, device and output options. Classic and anomaly tasks use their own independent environments. One of multiple NVIDIA GPUs can be selected; the current Windows implementation does not support joint multi-GPU training of one classic model. Use a small batch and few epochs to check paths, labels, GPU memory and outputs before full training. This workflow check does not assess final accuracy. After starting, use Console logs for charts and raw output. Charts show trends; raw logs show initialization, validation, export and error details. After successful training, inspect the automatically exported model. Classic training and export are separate stages; an export failure retains saved training weights. Open an experiment from Training history, or select a model for inference validation. Anomaly inference is on its own page. A task takes a parameter snapshot when started. Editing controls afterward does not change the running task; make changes before starting the next one. Closing the application asks for confirmation and defaults to cancel. Confirming exit while a task runs terminates it. Wait until training-file cleanup completes before exiting. Three runtime families ¶ Architecture Training method Device selection Four modern architectures Modern training engine auto / gpu / cpu; gpu uses GPU 0 Two classic architectures Independent classic environment CPU or any one selected NVIDIA GPU Anomaly detection Independent anomaly detection environment CPU or any one selected NVIDIA GPU After explicitly selecting GPU, a failure must not be interpreted as an automatic switch to CPU. Classic and anomaly tasks report errors when GPU is unavailable; inspect the log and environment.

docs.text: Training history and disk cleanup ¶ Training history lists four modern training tasks, two classic tasks and anomaly model building. Ordinary inference and runtime checks are excluded. New training runs automatically register their actual experiment paths. Common results locations are scanned by default; for older results elsewhere, click Add history directory and select the experiment folder or its parent. This registers the location without moving or copying training files. The list shows name, architecture, time, status, size and path, with architecture filters and text search. Select Open experiment folder or double-click a row. Hover to read truncated content. Older modern records without clear completion information show Status unknown, not training failure. Records with a known running state whose owning application has exited may show Run interrupted. Ordinary weight folders without native experiment metadata are not automatically treated as training experiments. What deletion does ¶ Delete record and training files removes the entire experiment folder , including checkpoints, exported models, logs and charts. Confirmation shows the full path and size and defaults to cancel. Deletion is irreversible. If the folder is already gone, only the index entry is removed. Cleanup is blocked while training, export or inference is running. During cleanup, new tasks cannot start and exit must wait for completion. Protective checks cover the program directory, runtime environments, datasets referenced by configurations, directory links and nested experiments. Files in use or insufficient permissions can cause partial cleanup failures; the record remains and an error is shown. A failure does not make already deleted files recoverable. Before proceeding, ensure models requiring long-term retention have independent copies. Space usage is the logical size of readable files and may differ from the bytes actually freed by the file system. The history index is stored in the current user's local application data and need not move with the installation directory.

docs.text: Model inference and automatic export ¶ Supported inference architectures ¶ Model inference supports all four modern tasks plus classic detection and classification. Use the anomaly page's own inference view for anomaly detection. Architecture Input weights What else is needed Modern models .pt or .onnx Matching task type; especially important for ONNX Classic detection/classification .pdparams Matching training YAML; it can be imported from an experiment The anomaly detection page itself model.patchcore.pt Image source, device and threshold multiplier on that page Importing a classic training experiment prioritizes the valid final configuration snapshot and actual checkpoint; a pretrained URL in YAML is not treated as a trained model. A class TXT can be specified if needed. Incompatible classic weight shapes cause an error rather than silently using random parameters. Task type, threshold and device ¶ Modern tasks include classification, object detection, instance segmentation and oriented object detection. For classic architectures, the selected architecture fixes the task type. The confidence field defaults to 0.3 and accepts 0.01–1.0. Detection inference retains results at or above the threshold; classic classification returns at most the top 5 classes meeting it. Native modern classification result handling does not filter class probabilities using this conf control ; it is not an OK/NG decision rule for modern classification. Modern PT follows the device selection. The current software forces modern ONNX inference to CPU , reporting this in the log even if GPU is selected; ONNX GPU inference is not guaranteed. Classic inference can use CPU or one selected NVIDIA GPU. Preprocessing ¶ Modern classification PT/ONNX models generated by the software embed center-crop preprocessing metadata, which software inference reads. External ONNX runtimes do not automatically apply preprocessing merely because a JSON file is nearby; deployment must implement it correctly. Classic classification reads the configured Infer preprocessing and class mapping; classic detection uses the matching TestReader. External weights without their training configuration cannot recover correct preprocessing from the file extension alone. Output directory ¶ Without an explicit output directory, the modern model task determines the default location. An explicitly selected directory is used directly and can be reused; results with identical names may be overwritten. Classic and anomaly inference create independent experiment directories beneath the output root, saving visualizations and structured results. The completion log provides the actual output path. Automatic training export ¶ Training architecture Export after success Four modern architectures ONNX; detection/segmentation/OBB also export infer_cfg.yml , while classification exports Label.txt and preprocessing information. Classic detection model.pdmodel , model.pdiparams , parameter information and infer_cfg.yml Classic classification Inference model, parameters, ImageSize.txt , deployment YAML and class list Anomaly detection Self-contained model.patchcore.pt ; use the anomaly inference workflow Modern ONNX export does not simplify the graph by default or automatically install onnxslim; OBB does not embed NMS. Classic export uses CPU within this run's independent process, even if training used GPU. The UI may continue to show Exporting after training finishes; wait for a confirmed export result before deployment. Training completion does not guarantee export completion. A failed classic export retains trained weights and the full experiment; inspect export.json and the raw log. Do not delete the entire experiment to retry export.

docs.text: Training charts and raw logs ¶ The console retains Training charts and Raw logs as separate views. Charts do not replace logs and never invent metrics that were not produced. Metrics by architecture ¶ Task Chart meaning Modern detection/segmentation/OBB Training and validation loss, actual detection evaluation metrics, learning rate Modern classification Classification loss, actual classification accuracy and learning rate Classic detection Training loss, actual validation results such as mAP, learning rate Classic classification Training/validation loss, actual accuracy and other metrics, learning rate Anomaly detection Feature and coreset sizes, calibration thresholds and time per construction stage; not gradient loss curves Without an independent validation set for classic COCO, the score panel states training only, no mAP calculation. With validation data, evaluation still follows the model configuration's interval, so values are not guaranteed every epoch. Valid zero values are retained; missing values are not filled with zero. Chart controls ¶ Hover over curves to inspect values; click legends to show or hide curves, drag a rectangle to zoom, and double-click to reset. You can export metric CSV, save chart PNG, open the experiment folder, and load historical JSONL/CSV metrics. Files such as training_metrics.jsonl generated during training can restore recorded values. If an older log did not save a metric, loading history does not rerun validation or infer accuracy from loss. Troubleshooting and task status ¶ After a failure, switch to raw logs and inspect the first actual exception with its context, not only the final exit code. Reaching the epoch limit, early stopping, user cancellation and errors are different states. Classic and anomaly experiments save engine.log . After an unexpected software exit, open the experiment directory from training history to read the saved log. Modern architectures usually also have results.csv , configuration and metric files; full UI raw logs are not guaranteed to survive process restarts. Use Export log to preserve the current console text. Serial training queue ¶ Click “Add to training queue” on any training page to capture the model, data paths and settings. Classic tasks also save the resolved YAML configuration. Later edits to the page or original YAML do not affect queued tasks. Images, annotations and weights are still read from their paths; do not move or replace them while tasks are pending. Use Training queue to start, reorder, duplicate or edit pending tasks. Only one task runs at a time; training, automatic export and resource cleanup must finish before the next starts. Pausing blocks subsequent tasks only. Stopping the current task also pauses the queue. Training failures pause by default, with an option to continue. Export failures always pause and are labeled as successful training with failed export. The queue is stored locally, and exiting still requires confirmation. After restart it remains paused; tasks that did not finish normally are marked as interrupted. Running again starts training from the beginning without automatic checkpoint resume. Removing a queue entry does not delete experiment files; use Training history to free disk space. Settings snapshots are viewed or edited as JSON. Only pending tasks can be edited, and each engine still validates paths and settings before execution.

docs.text: Environment and FAQ ¶ What to keep in the complete package ¶ Distribute the complete application folder, including the executable, _internal , classic runtimes and anomaly runtime. Customers need working GPU drivers and appropriate system runtime libraries; bundled framework libraries do not replace NVIDIA drivers. MkDocs is used only to build documentation during development. Customers do not need MkDocs, Python or a separate web server. The application starts a lightweight service bound only to the local machine; all five language editions and search resources are bundled. Bundled help lives in _internal/help_site ; keep it for the Help action. The root docs technical notes and package-manifest.json are still not training/inference dependencies. The manifest supports file-integrity diagnosis. Why mAP is missing ¶ First check for an independent validation set, then whether an evaluation epoch has been reached. Classic COCO training without validation does not split images or evaluate. If evaluation ran but yielded no valid metrics, inspect its raw logs; loss is not an evaluation substitute. Low GPU utilization ¶ GPU utilization depends on the task, batch size, image size, data loading, CPU preprocessing and sampling interval. GPU utilization and GPU memory usage are different measurements. Check that the logs show GPU execution and whether data_cost is large; for classic Windows training, adjust workers moderately and compare actual throughput. Insufficient RAM or GPU memory ¶ Reduce batch first, then image size as appropriate for the task. For anomaly detection, also reduce candidate-feature limits, coreset limits or the retention ratio. Parameters differ across tasks: a coreset limit is not a batch size. Classic models are still downloading pretrained weights ¶ Using pretrained settings from the configuration follows its URL; a customer machine may have no cached copy. Choose local compatible weights or random initialization offline. Having architecture files does not mean pretrained weights are cached. Mismatched weights, classes or preprocessing ¶ Use the same task, configuration, class order and preprocessing as the weights. Classic models can import their experiment settings; modern classification must retain preprocessing metadata. Do not use a horizontal detector as OBB or treat an exported classic static model as a .pdparams checkpoint. Why ONNX runs on CPU ¶ The main inference page currently forces modern ONNX models to use CPU and reports this in the raw log. Selecting GPU does not override this existing compatibility policy. Help pages or search cannot be opened ¶ Keep the application running, reopen Help from the sidebar, and check the default browser and local permissions. Internet is unnecessary. If files are missing, use a complete new package containing help_site ; adding documentation to source code does not update an old package automatically.

docs.text: Classic image classification 2.5.0 ¶ Classify the entire image. Presets currently include ResNet50, ResNet18, ResNet101, MobileNetV3_small_x0_35 and MobileNetV3_large_x1_0; entries appear only when their bundled configurations exist. Select one classification dataset folder. train_list.txt , val_list.txt and Label.txt take priority; without lists, train/class_name and val/class_name are recognized. Existing training/validation sets are retained without automatic resplitting. Verify class IDs and name order; training, inference and export must agree. Size and optimization ¶ The input is a square side length; 0 means Use configuration. A custom value updates training/validation crops, model input and export preprocessing. The Resize short edge follows the original classification ratio 256/224 rather than replacing all preprocessing with an uncropped stretch. Match the input size to the details needed by your application. This page has neither separate height/width controls nor the classic detection validation-only size mode. Learning rate, optimizer, weight decay, warmup, AMP and workers follow the classic common parameters , but map to the classification engine's configuration structure. Metrics ¶ Displays training and validation accuracy, loss and other metrics actually emitted by the classification engine. These must not be interpreted as detection Precision/Recall/mAP. Available metrics vary by model configuration; no curves are invented for missing values. Automatic export and deployment ¶ After training, automatic export writes to the experiment's export directory. Typical files are: inference.pdmodel inference.pdiparams inference.pdiparams.info ImageSize.txt inference_cls.yaml class_names.txt ImageSize.txt , class mapping and inference_cls.yaml are generated from this run's effective configuration. Customers need not replace generic ImageNet settings manually. The deployment YAML uses relative paths: use the export folder as the working directory and configure the deployment program's device for the actual hardware. Model inference validation uses the training checkpoint .pdparams and training configuration, rather than accepting an exported .pdmodel directly as this page's weight input. They serve different purposes. See the classification parameter table for all controls.

docs.text: Classic common parameters and independent environments ¶ Classic object detection uses ATSLegacy 2.7.0 ; classic classification uses ATSLegacy 2.5.0 . These identify architecture/configuration versions, not modern architecture versions. The pages share some controls, but implement dataset preprocessing and parameter mapping separately. Override priority ¶ Load the selected model YAML and its base configurations, generate a separate experiment configuration, then apply explicit UI overrides. Built-in YAML files are not rewritten. Use configuration preserves the original setting, not a universal fixed default. Epochs, batch size and random seed use the UI values directly, defaulting to 100, 4 and 42 respectively; other optimization settings default to the model configuration. Each experiment saves effective_det.yaml or effective_clas.yaml to verify actual sizes, data paths, classes, learning rate and loader settings. Weight initialization ¶ Option Actual behavior Use pretrained settings from the configuration Uses the YAML setting; a URL may download weights or hit an existing cache. A cache is not guaranteed on every customer's computer. Use local pretrained weights Specify a compatible .pdparams for initialization in this run. This is not a resume-training switch. Random initialization Do not load the configuration's pretrained weights; start from random parameters. A valid model configuration is still required. Offline, choose local weights or random initialization. The presence of an architecture folder alone does not mean pretrained weights are included. Learning rate and optimizer ¶ An initial-learning-rate UI value of 0 means Use configuration; it does not set the engine learning rate to 0. The weight-decay Use configuration placeholder likewise makes no override. Keep the configured optimizer or explicitly select Momentum, SGD, Adam or AdamW. The application adapts parameter structures when switching; AdamW receives numeric weight decay rather than the previous optimizer's regularizer dictionary. Learning-rate schedule Behavior Use configuration setting Preserve milestones, total schedule length and warmup. Changing the training epoch count does not automatically rewrite the whole schedule. Constant learning rate Uses the initial learning rate of this run's configuration, without UI-configured warmup. Cosine annealing Rebuilds the schedule for this run's total epochs. Warmup epochs must be an integer smaller than the total. Match training length and schedule If the reference schedule was designed for 80 or 96 epochs and this run lasts 300, Use configuration may decay the learning rate to its minimum before training finishes. To align the schedule with this run, choose cosine and inspect the effective YAML. Data augmentation and AMP ¶ Keeping model augmentation preserves its original policy. Disabling random augmentation substitutes validation preprocessing for random training augmentation. Normalization, channel layout and required resizing remain. AMP can follow the configuration, be disabled, or be enabled. Explicit enabling requires a GPU; CPU training disables AMP. Following the configuration does not guarantee AMP on a GPU: the model configuration still decides. Windows workers and GPU selection ¶ Native multiprocessing data loading is limited in the classic Windows runtime. With workers>0 , this application uses threads inside the isolated process for parallel reading and preprocessing; 0 keeps the original loader. Start with 2 or 4; a larger value is not necessarily faster. Each task uses one selected NVIDIA GPU; any installed card can be selected, but native Windows multi-GPU joint training of one classic model is not supported. The independent process normally reports GPU 0 because of visible-device mapping; this does not mean the physical card selection was ignored. Each run creates an independent timestamped directory under the output root. Training and automatic export use the independent classic environment without changing modern or anomaly environments. See the parameter checklist for complete ranges.

docs.text: Classic object detection 2.7.0 ¶ For standard object detection. The model list shows s / m / l / x / sod ; SOD uses the actual small-object model configuration, not simply a smaller input size for an ordinary model. Train from one COCO folder ¶ Select a COCO folder and click Check dataset to verify classes and training/validation image counts. The software generates data configuration within the experiment; manually editing the built-in coco_detection file is unnecessary. Unannotated OK images participate as negative background samples. Without a separate validation set, all training samples are retained: no automatic split, validation or mAP calculation occurs. Loss and learning rate still appear; this is not a training failure. The advanced Use YAML dataset configuration option retains the model file's dataset settings; users must ensure correct paths and classes. Relative paths are resolved from the classic detection working directory, not automatically from an arbitrary external YAML's directory. Height and width: three modes ¶ Size mode Training Validation, testing and export Use model size settings Preserve the reference configuration, including multi-scale training Preserve the reference configuration Fixed size Use the specified height × width and disable random size selection Use the same height × width Customize validation and export size only Preserve the original training size strategy Use the specified height × width Enter height and width separately; both must be 96–8192 and multiples of 32. Custom sizes directly resize images without preserving the original aspect ratio. For height 320 and width 640, select the third mode to reproduce changing only eval_height=320 and eval_width=640 . Training may still randomly select square sizes from the original configuration; it does not become 320×640 . Select the second mode if training must also use this fixed rectangle. If random augmentation is also disabled, training preprocessing changes accordingly; the size mode does not re-enable disabled augmentation. Validation metrics ¶ With an independent validation set, evaluation runs at the model configuration's validation interval; metrics are not guaranteed every epoch. Charts show actual detection evaluation results such as mAP50-95, mAP50 and mAP75. Classification accuracy is not a general detection metric on this page. No validation set, validation not yet due, and validation with no valid results are different states, shown separately in the charts. Missing values are not filled with 0; an actually computed 0 is retained. Automatic export ¶ After training, a saved checkpoint is selected automatically and the official inference export is run. After success, export/export_det in the experiment usually contains: model.pdmodel model.pdiparams model.pdiparams.info infer_cfg.yml The export-completed log gives the actual path. infer_cfg.yml stores effective preprocessing and classes; custom dimensions are reflected in exported inputs and preprocessing. Export runs on CPU even when training used a GPU. For other optimizer, loader and initialization settings, see classic common parameters ; all controls are in the detection parameter table . Evaluate on training set ¶ Unchecked by default. In COCO mode, selecting this option evaluates all training images and annotations in place of a separate validation set, without automatic splitting or changes to the original data. Training data is used even when a separate validation set is available. This option is disabled when using YAML dataset settings. AP/mAP on the training set reflects only the fit to that data and does not measure generalization to new images. Evaluation follows the interval in the model configuration. docs.text: Modern image classification ¶ Classify the whole image without boxes or masks. Organize images in class folders. Defaults: input 960, maximum epochs 500, batch 8, workers 4, AdamW, initial learning rate 0.0005 and final multiplier 0.01. Rotation and flipping ¶ degrees defaults to 180, the maximum absolute random rotation during training; 0 disables this rotation. The application removes RandAugment's duplicate Rotate operation and inserts an explicit rotation to keep its strength controlled. Vertical and horizontal flip probabilities both default to 0.5. Center-crop fraction crop_fraction ¶ This is a retention fraction defined on the image's short edge, not object-box cropping or random image deletion. For example, with imgsz=960 and fraction 0.8 , resize the short edge to at least 960/0.8=1200 , then center-crop 960×960 . Validation and software inference use the same rule; training still applies random cropping and other augmentations after this central-region preprocessing. At a fraction of 1, the short edge is not additionally enlarged, but validation/inference still center-crops to a square and can remove the edges of elongated images. A fraction of 1 does not preserve every edge for all aspect ratios. The fraction and preprocessing rules are written to PT and ONNX metadata. ONNX also generates .preprocess.json for external deployment reference; software inference prioritizes embedded model information. Older models without this metadata retain native preprocessing and are not retroactively modified. Outputs and metrics ¶ Results are stored in a sibling folder named after the dataset with the _runs suffix. Charts show actual classification metrics such as accuracy, not detection mAP. Typical outputs include best.pt , last.pt , deployment PT, ONNX, class Label.txt and preprocessing information; the successful export log is authoritative. See modern common parameters and the classification parameter table for other controls.

docs.text: Modern common parameters and augmentation ¶ The four tasks share basic parameters, but not every augmentation applies to every task. Actual controls and defaults are listed in the parameter reference . Basic parameters ¶ Parameter Function and usage Model weights Select preset weights matching the task. Classification, detection, segmentation and OBB weights are not freely interchangeable. imgsz A single input size. Detection/segmentation/OBB resize and pad according to engine rules; classification additionally uses its own short-edge resize and crop. epochs Maximum epochs, not a guaranteed number of completed epochs. patience Consecutive epochs without validation metric improvement before early stopping; 0 disables it. Reaching epochs normally is not early stopping. batch Images per batch; increasing this generally uses more GPU memory and does not guarantee proportional speedup. workers Number of data loader processes; 0 loads in the main process. Defaults: input 640, maximum epochs 1000, batch size 16, workers 0 to reduce Windows data loading compatibility issues. Enable parallel loading according to your actual environment when needed. Do not confuse the two angle controls: Parameter Meaning degrees Maximum absolute rotation angle for training image augmentation angle Model angle loss weight, default 1; not a rotation angle This page does not show standard detection copy-paste or background erasing controls.
